problem:
A numerical method is used to approximate the solution to an initial value problem.

- With step size $Δx=0.12,$ the observed global truncation error is $e(0.12)=0.310.$

- With step size $Δx=0.06,$ the observed global truncation error is $e(0.06)=0.078.$

Use this data to estimate the order of the numerical method.

feedback.problem:
The global truncation error (GTE) of a numerical method with step size $Δx$ is

$$
e(Δx)=5(Δx)^{4}-(Δx)^{5}.
$$

Complete the following sentences.$\,$ With step size $Δx=0.7,$ the global truncation error is $≈$
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ With step size $Δx=0.2,$ the global truncation error is $≈$
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Decreasing from $Δx=0.7$ to $Δx=0.2,$ the GTE is reduced by a factor of $≈$
{{field-3}}.

$\,$ According to this data, the order of the method is approximately
{{field-4}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
A numerical method has order $p$ if $p$ is the largest positive integer such that the global truncation error (GTE) satisfies

$$
e(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{p})\,\text{as}\,Δx\to 0.
$$

The order describes how fast errors shrink as $Δx$ decreases.

In other words, a numerical method has order $p$ if, for sufficiently small step sizes, reducing the step size by a factor of $k$ reduces the GTE by a factor of approximately ${k}^{p}.$

First, we compute the GTE for the given step sizes:

- With step size $Δx=0.7,$ the GTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}e(0.7) & =5(0.7)^{4}-(0.7)^{5} \\  & =5\cdot 0.2401-1\cdot 0.168\,07 \\  & =1.200\,5-0.168\,07 \\  & =1.032\,43 \\  & ≈1.032.\end{aligned}
$$

- With step size $Δx=0.2,$ the GTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}e(0.2) & =5(0.2)^{4}-(0.2)^{5} \\  & =5\cdot 0.001\,6-1\cdot 0.000\,32 \\  & =0.008-0.000\,32 \\  & =0.007\,68 \\  & ≈0.008.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the order by comparing the errors. The step size decreases from $0.7$ to $0.2.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
k=\frac{0.7}{0.2}=3.5.
$$

As a result, for a numerical method of order $p,$ the GTE should decrease by a factor of approximately

$$
{k}^{p}=(3.5)^{p}.
$$

On the other hand, the GTE actually decreases from $1.032\,43$ to $0.007\,68.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
\frac{1.032\,43}{0.007\,68}=134.430\,99…≈134.431.
$$

Comparing the two scale factors for the GTE, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(3.5)^{p} & ≈134.430\,99… \\ p & ≈{log}_{3.5}⁡(134.430\,99…) \\ p & ≈3.912….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, rounding to the nearest integer, the estimated order of the method is
$4.$

Indeed, this coincides with the definition of the order from the expression for the GTE:

$$
e(Δx)=5(Δx)^{4}-(Δx)^{5}\,⇒\,e(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{4})\,\text{as}\,Δx\to 0.
$$

Hence, the order of the method is $4.$
